sections.text:
In a quiet lake, there lived a kind turtle, but he complained and talked a lot.

She loved her two teal friends who visited her every summer.

The turtle was looking at the two ducks as they were flying in the high sky with regret, and said: “I wish I could fly like you and see the world from above! I am a prisoner of this slow shell and small lake!”

At the end of the summer, the two ducks announced that they would migrate to the warm south because the lake would soon freeze over.

The turtle cried and said: “Please take me with you. I will die here of cold and loneliness!”

The two ducks thought for a long time, and one of them said: “We have a very clever idea! We will bring a strong wooden stick, you will hold the middle firmly in your mouth, and we will hold both ends with our beaks and fly you into the sky!”

But the duck warned her sternly: “You must promise never to open your mouth, no matter what happens or what you hear, because if you speak, you will fall and break your shell!”

The turtle agreed and swore that he would not say a word, and bit down on the stick with all his might.

The two ducks flew into the sky and carried the turtle with them, and the experience was amazing for the turtle, who saw rivers, mountains, and villages from above for the first time in his life.

They passed over a small village, and the peasants and children saw this strange sight: two ducks carrying a turtle flying!
People started shouting and gesticulating with their hands: “Wow! A turtle is flying! What a genius idea from these clever ducks!”

The turtle felt angry and arrogant, and wanted to tell them that the idea was thanks to her intelligence, not the ducks!
The turtle completely forgot the promise and warning, and opened his mouth to scream, saying: “It was my idea, you idiot.

".

As soon as she opened her mouth to speak, the stick slipped from her jaw, and she fell from the high sky like a heavy stone, shattering her shell on the solid rocks of the earth and killing her.

Thus, everyone learned that chatter and the inability to remain silent and keep covenants in critical times, along with a little arrogance, may lead a person to inevitable and devastating destruction.
